subject: SLO calibration and reproducibility: prompt pack + harness asks
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quickcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: latency/throughput goals + reproducibility asks

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful read on QuickCart's production constraints. Summarizing the perf-oriented asks we agreed to validate so we can move to a focused qualification run: 

- Target latency SLOs: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for short-form SKU lookups (prompt ~25 tokens).
- Long-form completions (order summarization) target: p50 <= 500ms, p95 <= 1.2s.
- Concurrency / throughput: baseline 80 concurrent active sessions, with burst capacity to 300 concurrent for 90s windows. Sustained QPS target: 120 qps over a 10-minute window.
- Streaming behavior: client expects chunked delivery (first token within 150ms for short prompts) and token-by-token flushes; we need to reproduce via SSE/websocket harness.

What we'd like from you to run a reproducible benchmark: 
1) A representative prompt set (250 examples) that covers short SKU queries, cart-abandonment flows, and two-step compose completions. Please include expected reference outputs where possible.
2) A traffic profile (concurrency and inter-arrival distribution) — if you can share a short .csv with timestamps or a sample k6/Locust script that matches production bursts, that would be ideal.
3) Clarify whether tokenization should be measured on raw input or after client-side pre-processing.

We attached a suggested SLO matrix (slo_matrix_qc.xlsx) and a template prompt pack (quickcart_prompt_pack_v1.txt) with our initial sampling. If any of these are off the mark, let us know and we will iterate.

Next steps / timeline request: if you can share the prompt set + traffic profile by EOD Monday (Jun 14), we can schedule a reproducibility run with our eval harness on Wed (Jun 16) and share a protocol + artifacts the same day.

Thanks — Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: quickcart_prompt_pack_v1.txt (text), slo_matrix_qc.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quickcart.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Park <chris.park@quickcart.com>, Dev Ops <devops@quickcart.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency/throughput goals + reproducibility asks

Hi Mateo — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 target for short SKU lookups is a hard requirement for checkout UX — anything above 350ms drives a measurable abandonment bump. We understand tail behavior can differ with batching, so we want clear guidance on config that meets p95 while keeping cost acceptable.
- For streaming, our client expects an initial token within 100–150ms for SKU lookups (they render first partial suggestion). For longer completions the first token can be slower (<= 350ms), but we need steady streaming thereafter.
- Prompt tokenization: we pre-process (strip metadata headers) before sending; measure from request send (post-preprocess) to first-byte and to last-byte.

We're attaching a 200-sample prompt set (we'll also upload the full 250 by Monday) and a short k6 script that approximates our 3pm daily traffic spike.

Two quick asks: 
1) Can you confirm the exact definitions you will use for TTFB and end-to-end latency in the run so our DevOps team can line up observability instrumentation?
2) Will the harness simulate streaming over both SSE and websocket? One of our web clients is SSE-only.

I'll upload the prompt pack and the k6 artifact to the Drive link you sent.

—Laura

Attachments referenced: quickcart_prompt_pack_partial_200.txt, qc_k6_spike.js
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@quickcart.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency/throughput goals + reproducibility asks

Laura — looping in a perf engineer on our side and clarifying measurement defs up-front. Quick answers: 

- Measurement definitions we will use in the harness: 
  * TTFB (time-to-first-byte): delta between request transmit completion at client and receipt of first model byte at client socket. For streaming tests this is measured per request (first token latency).
  * E2E (end-to-end / completion latency): time from request transmit completion to final closing token event. For streaming runs we will also capture inter-token latency distribution (mean inter-token, 95th percentile inter-token).
  * Observability mapping: we will emit both client-side synthetic metrics and server-side trace spans; we will provide a mapping table (trace-span IDs -> measurement metric) before the run.

- Harness behavior: our redwood-eval-harness v1.3 supports both SSE and websocket streaming, and will replay the k6 inter-arrival profile against a pinned model variant. It also supports optional prefix cache warmup and KV-cache preloading to reproduce steady-state behavior for conversational flows.

Please note: to reproduce p95 tails we need the full 250 prompt set (particularly the long-order summarization examples). If you can push that by Monday morning we can reserve Wed morning for a first reproducibility pass.

I'll follow up with a short measurement spec that maps to the columns you likely want in your dashboards (ttfb_ms, e2e_ms, intertoken_p50_ms, intertoken_p95_ms, cpu_gpu_util, mem_gb).

—Ben

Thanks everyone — quick status and action items before the Wed run: 

- Laura / QuickCart: please upload the remaining 50 prompts (finalized 250 pack) and confirm whether the k6 script should include TLS variation (we saw some production clients use short-lived TLS sessions).
- Mateo: will stage the pinned model (gpt-qa-redwood-1.0-int8) and run a cache-warmup pass before the formal measurement window.
- Ben: please push the measurement spec (CSV schema + span->metric mapping) by Monday EOD so QuickCart can align dashboards.
- Marissa: I'll schedule a 30-minute pre-run check-in Tuesday 09:00 PT to confirm harness flags and security/endpoint details (VPC peering token to be exchanged 24 hours prior).

Deliverables we'll share after the run: raw harness logs, per-request CSV of TTFB/E2E/inter-token latency, and a short readout deck with cost delta estimates for different batching and quantization knobs.

Marissa Cole
